unit.title: Public Goods, Taxes, and Community Choices

contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned about goods, services, and trade. This week: how a whole community pays for some things together!

A private good is something one person or family buys for themselves, like a toy or a bike. A public good is something the whole community pays for together, so everyone can use it — like a public park, a public library, or a fire department. Sort these into public or private: a video game, a public library, a family's car, a public playground. Explain why a fire department has to be a public good instead of something each family buys separately.
You just learned the difference between public and private goods! Tomorrow we'll learn exactly how public goods get paid for: taxes.

objectives: Distinguish a private good (bought individually) from a public good (paid for by the whole community)
Explain why some goods and services, like a fire department, work better as public goods
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's goods/services/trade vocabulary briefly.
2. Introduce public vs. private goods with the park/library vs. toy/bike examples.
3. Have the child sort the 4 example items into public or private.
4. Discuss the fire-department question together.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's taxes lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a simple test question — 'could just one family buy this for only themselves?' — to sort each example
Ready for more: ask the child to name one more public good and one more private good from their own life
The fire-department example is the strongest one for building genuine understanding — spend extra time there if the sorting activity feels easy
teacherGuide.answerKey: Public: public library, public playground. Private: video game, family's car. A fire department is public because everyone needs to be protected, and most families couldn't afford their own fire truck and firefighters.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's Economics dimension (public vs. private goods) at a Grade 2 level, opening this week's community-choices thread building on last week's goods/services foundation.
